title: The long peace is broken. The Pope proclaims a crusade against al-Andalus, the first, and declares war on the Ṭāʾifa of Aragon; the Emperor answers for his subject. The crusade's temporal support is thin: the Pope's own vassals and a handful of German bishops and princes, some five thousand men at the declaration, most of them levies

data.target: ARA (the Borja Sultanate of Aragon, as the game styles it)

crusaders.Papal States: 270 men under arms on 3 February (four regiments far under strength: crossbowmen at 10%, men-at-arms at 5%), 26 ships; the Pope's manpower pool stood near 2,000

defenders.the ṭāʾifas: Aragon, Catalonia (400), Valencia (450), the Algarve, Salamanca, Cuenca
defenders.Mamlūks: 4,050 men, with Mecca, Medina, the Dulkadirids, Hutaym, Barqa, Banū Kanz, Suakin, the Western Oases, Val di Noto, Zubāla, Nafūsa and others
defenders.Morocco: 2,400 men, 30 ships, with Tafilalt, Touat and Tlemcen

data.peace: the first war since the Peace of Ramaḍān in 1395, nearly nine years

source: save of 3 February 1404; Trent's account and screen

title: Eight days into the crusade the papal fleet, seven sail, catches two Catalan ships in the Gulf of Roses and sinks both
source: save of 22 October 1404 (the war's battle list)

title: At Aix-en-Provence 373 Sienese crusaders attack the Catalan army of 4,800 and are wiped out without a Catalan loss
source: save of 22 October 1404 (the war's battle list)

title: At the mouths of the Rhône the papal fleet of seven fights the Algarve's seven to a draw, and the Algarve loses one ship
source: save of 22 October 1404 (the war's battle list)

title: The joined fleets of Catalonia and Morocco, ninety-one sail, find a lone papal ship at the mouths of the Rhône and sink it
source: save of 22 October 1404 (the war's battle list)

title: France grants al-Andalus military access, and on 4 July the armies of the faithful march through Languedoc on Avignon, the Pope's city on the Rhône. The Emperor, fifty-six, crosses the border at their head

data.target: Avignon, the papal enclave on the Rhône
data.context: France had shown itself friendly since 1395; the Pope's own lands in Italy lie across the sea

title: In the Gulf of Saint-Florent off Corsica the Moroccan fleet, sixty-five sail under Abū Ḥammū, sinks a papal squadron of five to the last ship
source: save of 22 October 1404 (the war's battle list)

title: At the mouths of the Rhône the Catalan fleet of twenty-six attacks the last three papal ships and is beaten off, losing four
source: save of 22 October 1404 (the war's battle list)

title: In the gulf of Talamone the papal remnant of three attacks sixteen ships of Barqa and Noto and is driven off; each side loses one
source: save of 22 October 1404 (the war's battle list)

title: The Sephardim of al-Mariyya. Jews from across Iberia have made the town of al-Mariyya a haven, where they live without persecution. Some at court welcome it as equality for all of Allāh's creation; the zealous call it a stain on the empire. The Emperor, in the field before Avignon, rules that the rights of the Jewish people shall be protected, and the crown builds them a community house at al-Mariyya

data.choice: We shall protect the rights of the Jewish people (the option on Trent's screen)

effects.construction: a Jewish Community building in al-Mariyya

data.alternative: Allāh would never allow these unbelievers to live in peace!
data.context: the convivencia proclaimed with the Restoration of al-Andalus in 1375; some 123,000 Jews in the realm in 1395. At the time the Emperor was besieging Avignon, and the crusade's war score stood at +40%

title: At Barjols in Provence the Valencian army of 2,700 attacks a papal army of 1,300 and is thrown back, losing 1,295 for 784
source: save of 22 October 1404 (the war's battle list)

title: Ten days later the Emperor himself comes up with 4,900 and destroys what is left of the papal army at Barjols, 495 of its 519 men, for the loss of four
source: save of 22 October 1404 (the war's battle list)

title: Avignon, the Pope's city on the Rhône, is in the Emperor's hands: the save of 22 October shows it controlled by al-Andalus

data.note: the day of the fall is not in the save

title: The Peace of Avignon. With his army destroyed at Barjols and his city in the Emperor's hands, the Pope gives up his crusade. He is humiliated before Christendom, pays 585 in gold at once and war reparations after. No land changes hands

battleDead.ourSide: 1,299 men in the land battles (1,295 of them Valencians at Barjols), and 8 ships
battleDead.theirSide: 1,652 men in the land battles, and 7 ships

alsoInTheSave.casusBelli: since 2 May 1404 the court has been preparing a new claim, the Reconquest of Iberia, against Castile
alsoInTheSave.france: France grants food access as well as military access (from 5 August 1404)
